2027-02-16.title: Second Tuesday of the Great Fast
2027-02-16.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The glory that is to be revealed
2027-02-16.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba).
2027-02-16.verse: “Ask, and it will be given you; search, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened for you.
theo: February in Kerala is the beginning of the hot months. The paddy fields of the Kole lands and Kuttanad lie dry after the harvest, the wells begin to fall, and by the afternoon the whole land seems to wait for a rain that will not come until the summer showers. Paul gives words to that waiting. “I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing with the glory about to be revealed to us. For the creation waits with eager longing for the revealing of the children of God.” Creation was subjected to futility, “in hope that the creation itself will be set free from its bondage to decay and will obtain the freedom of the glory of the children of God.” Then comes one of the boldest images in Scripture: “We know that the whole creation has been groaning in labor pains until now.” The groan of the world is not the cry of a dying thing, but of a mother about to give birth.

We groan too. “And not only the creation, but we ourselves, who have the first fruits of the Spirit, groan inwardly while we wait for adoption, the redemption of our bodies.” The Great Fast teaches us to feel this groan honestly. When we are hungry in the late afternoon, when a habit we have given up pulls at us, when prayer feels dry, we are standing with the whole creation in its labour. Paul does not call this despair; he calls it hope. “For in hope we were saved. Now hope that is seen is not hope. For who hopes for what is seen? But if we hope for what we do not see, we wait for it with patience.” Many parishes hold their Lenten retreat, the dhyanam, in these weeks, and families come back from those days of listening with the same discovery: the waiting itself is a school of hope.

Into this waiting Jesus speaks his invitation to pray. “Ask, and it will be given you; search, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened for you.” He is not describing a vending machine, but a father. “Is there anyone among you who, if your child asks for bread, will give a stone? Or if the child asks for a fish, will give a snake? If you then, who are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask him!” The Father does not always give what we name, but he never gives a stone for bread. And the same passage ends with the golden rule: “In everything do to others as you would have them do to you; for this is the law and the prophets.” The one who knocks at God's door learns to open his own door to others.
outline: Ask: what are you waiting for, and how do you wait?
The groan of the world is a birth pang.
We wait with patience for what we do not see.
A Father who never gives a stone for bread.
The one who knocks learns to open.
“Ask, and it will be given you; search, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened for you.”
live: Choose one intention and bring it to God every day for the rest of the Great Fast, without giving up.
Each evening this week, ask: did I treat someone today as I would want to be treated?
Save water this summer and share it generously with neighbours whose wells run dry.
2027-02-16.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, with the whole creation we groan and wait for the glory to come. Teach us to hope for what we do not see and to wait for it with patience. You told us to ask, to search and to knock; give us the confidence of children before the Father who never gives a stone for bread, and make us generous to others as we want them to be to us. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the Father gives us the true bread from heaven; we receive in hope the first fruits of the glory that is still to be revealed.

quick: Creation groans like a mother in labour; glory is coming.
We are saved in hope and wait with patience.
Ask, search, knock: the Father never gives a stone for bread.
2027-02-16.action: Bring one intention to God today and promise to keep asking until Easter.
2027-02-16.question: Do I pray like a child who trusts the Father, or like a stranger who expects to be refused?

family.explain: Jesus says: if a child asks his father for bread, the father will not give him a stone. God is a much better Father than any father on earth. He hears us when we ask. Sometimes he gives exactly what we ask, sometimes something better, but always what is good for us.
family.intention: We pray for children who are hungry and have no one to give them bread.
family.ask: Ask: “What shall we ask God for together, every day until Easter?”

illus: A boy in Muvattupuzha begged his father all one summer for a ride on the new motorbike out on the highway. The father kept saying no, and every evening took him instead for a long walk to the river, where they talked about school and friends. The boy sulked for weeks. Twenty years later, at his father's funeral, he told the parish that those evening walks were the best gift his father ever gave him. He had asked for speed; his father gave him time.

pm.open: Heavenly Father, we come to you as children. We ask, we search, we knock. Open to us. Amen.
share: Creation waits with eager longing (Romans 8:19). Where do I see the world groaning around me?
In hope we were saved (Romans 8:24). What helps me to wait with patience?
Ask, and it will be given you (Matthew 7:7). What have I stopped asking God for, and why?
pm.resp: Father, give good things to those who ask you.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a people of hope.
For farmers and families facing water shortage in the summer months.
For those who have stopped praying because they feel unheard.
For all who are making a Lenten retreat these weeks.
For our group, that we may do to others as we would have them do to us.
pm.close: Father, you hear the groaning of your creation and the prayers of your children. Fill us with hope, teach us to ask with confidence, and make us generous to everyone. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Saint Paul says that the whole creation has been groaning in labour pains until now (Romans 8:22). In these hot February days, when the fields are dry and the wells begin to fall, we can almost hear that groan. But it is the groan of a mother about to give birth, not of something dying.

We too groan as we wait. In this fast we feel hunger, we feel the pull of the habits we have given up. Paul says: in hope we were saved; and if we hope for what we do not see, we wait for it with patience (Romans 8:24–25).

Jesus teaches us how to wait: by prayer. Ask, and it will be given you; search, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened for you (Matthew 7:7). Our Father in heaven will never give us a stone when we ask for bread. He may not give what we name, but he always gives what is good.
And he ends with the golden rule: do to others as you would have them do to you (Matthew 7:12). Let us knock at God's door this week, and open our own door to others. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says: ask, and you will receive. God is a good Father who loves to give good things. What will you ask him for today? And what good thing will you give to someone else?

intro: Theme: “Ask, and it will be given you; search, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened for you.”
The groaning of creation, the patience of hope, and the Father who gives good things to those who ask.

sub: A birth pang, not a death rattle.
q: For I am about to create new heavens and a new earth; the former things shall not be remembered or come to mind.
We know that the whole creation has been groaning in labor pains until now;
points.apply: Do one concrete thing this week to care for God's creation, especially water.

points.apply: When the fast feels hard, offer that moment to God as an act of hope.

concl: Creation groans and we groan with it, but it is the groan of a birth.
Ask the Father with confidence, and do to others as you would have them do to you.
2027-02-16.resolve: Pray every day until Easter for one intention, and do one unasked kindness each day this week.
